name: Sanctions & coercion
value: EU weighs IRGC cyber sanctions; FMs meet 16 Nov
summary: EU foreign ministers meet on 16 Nov to discuss sanctions after France blamed an IRGC unit for attacks on ~700 shops
state: France said on 10 Nov that the Shahid Kaveh cyber unit, linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guards, attacked refrigeration controls at about 700 commercial sites on 11–12 Oct, summoned Iran's ambassador and warned of sanctions (Rudaw). EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas has proposed new sanctions on those responsible, for discussion by foreign ministers on 16 Nov (Demócrata). Searches on 15 Nov found no major economy cut off from payment systems and no large seizure of sovereign assets, so Watch holds.
for_you: Firms trading with Iran or handling Iranian-linked parties are exposed to new EU listings. UK businesses can check current designations on the UK sanctions list published by the FCDO and OFSI.
rubric_hit: Watch: major new sanctions packages under discussion (EU on Iran, 16 Nov); no payment-system cut-off or sovereign-asset seizure

sources.title: Rudaw — France accuses Iran's IRGC of cyberattacks on supermarkets
Demócrata — Kallas proposes new sanctions against Iran for cyberattacks on European supermarkets

why: Sanctions are now a frontline weapon; secondary sanctions and asset seizures fragment global finance and trade.
drivers: Russia/Iran sanctions packages, secondary sanctions, frozen-asset decisions, export controls.
